curvature?"}],"feedback_interpretation":"The latest labels weakened several inherited model-based extrapolations. m129 at 2/1 and 10/1 was moderate, rejecting direct transfer of the very late m128 response and motivating a local m129 curve. m115 was also much flatter than predicted across its selected ratio pair. In contrast, m36, m19, m107, m191, and m199 exposed substantial scaffold-specific endpoint errors: m36 and m19 were late relative to prediction, m107 and m191 showed steep V2 growth, and m199 confirmed a strong sulfoxide transition at 5/1. The m80 midpoint remained ordinary, so the predicted interior hump is now weak evidence. Loading contrasts from m60, m87, m119, and m200 continue to support separate V1 and V2 loading effects. I therefore prioritize local response curves and threshold locations, while retaining m91 as an ordinary diester control and avoiding a global tail correction.","batch_rationale":"The batch is organized around interpretable local experiments. m129, m115, m36, and m19 repair newly exposed transfer failures with strong-eluent baselines, midpoints, and loading contrasts. m107, m205, m191, and m72 sample threshold-like tail families at matched or near-matched loadings, giving the retrained model information about curvature and separate onset/completion behavior. m199 provides a sulfur-oxygen interaction series around a confirmed large discrepancy. m91 supplies an ordinary unsaturated-diest er control against overgeneralizing late retention from oxygen count, while m87 and m89 extend condition and loading response coverage in aromatic ester families. The batch contains connected measurements rather than redundant extreme predictions, and its labels should improve generalization by teaching scaffold-condition interactions, endpoint-specific loading effects, and calibration across both ordinary and late Row-distribution regimes."}
